clue.text: Lever end off pack (some chocolate?)

indicators.note: with its end off, the word for a pack loses its final letter

blocks.note: a pack of people is a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone levers the end off a pack, hoping to find some chocolate inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a bar is only one form chocolate comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron tool used to prise things apart, a kind of lever.

clue.text: Get down right inside sofa

indicators.note: the single letter sits within the piece of furniture

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb off the furniture and sit properly on the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: To crouch is to bend low with knees drawn up, lowering the body close to the ground.

clue.text: Start to thump eccentric

blocks.note: the off is the start of a race

explanation.surface: An odd character suddenly begins hitting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or unusual, describing a person or idea that is quirky and strange.

clue.text: Rhymes in reverse

definitions.note: cryptic: the answer is made of two words that chime

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: the answer's two halves share their sound
second meaning: to go back the way one came

explanation.walkthrough: BACK and TRACK rhyme, so the answer itself is a pair of rhymes; the surface suggests a poem written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To backtrack is to retrace one's steps or withdraw from a position, a retreat in direction or opinion.

clue.text: Personnel supporting sport in Dortmund area

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece is placed underneath the other

blocks.note: HR is human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: Staff are backing a local team in a German football city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is the industrial region of western Germany in which Dortmund is one of the major cities.

clue.text: In darkness, makes cuts in middle of speech

indicators.note: the middle of a six-letter word is its central pair of letters
the cutting word is placed in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: the two central letters of speech

explanation.surface: An editor working in the dark trims the middle out of someone's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speech' has six letters, so its middle is two letters, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse is the obscuring of the sun or moon, a blotting out of light that brings darkness.

clue.text: For church unity Alice originally entertains Christian Union types

indicators.note: the name is not in its original form, so its letters are rearranged
a host entertains guests within, so the other letters go inside

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the student society
types in the sense of fellows or chaps

explanation.surface: A woman named Alice hosts members of a student Christian society, in the cause of church unity.
explanation.walkthrough: ALICE is jumbled to E...ICAL, holding CU and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical describes efforts to bring together the different Christian denominations into a single fellowship.

clue.text: Sort of printer that turns up in fire sale

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words that follow
in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of the two words

explanation.surface: A printer surfaces at a clearance sale of fire-damaged goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer is a common office machine that uses a beam of light to transfer toner onto paper.

clue.text: Even out till the early hours, apostle briefly pops round

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the apostle loses his final letter
the shortened apostle goes around the other piece

blocks.note: staying up till the early hours is staying up late

explanation.surface: An apostle drops by and stays up into the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even out' reads like a verb phrase about smoothing, and it is: the answer is used as a verb meaning level off.
explanation.definitionFit: To plateau is to level off after a period of growth, reaching a steady state rather than rising further.

clue.text: Plea to have dinner in lobby

indicators.note: the eating goes inside the entrance hall

blocks.note: an entry is an entrance hall
to have dinner is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone begs to be allowed to eat in the hotel foyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or appeal, a heartfelt begging for something.

clue.text: Terce and sext for example, or a longer stretch of the day

definitions.text: a longer stretch of the day

blocks.note: terce and sext are canonical hours of the church's daily prayer cycle, the divine office

blocks.clueFragment: a longer stretch of the day
blocks.note: the working day, typically nine to five

explanation.walkthrough: Terce (mid-morning) and sext (midday) are short monastic prayer services; the phrase also names the normal working day, which is much longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours of the divine office are fixed prayer times, while in ordinary speech the phrase means regular business working time.

clue.text: Fitting carpet that’s oddly defective

indicators.note: defective in its odd places means the first, third and fifth letters are missing, leaving the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of carpet

explanation.surface: A shopper complains that the fitted carpet has some strange defects.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt and fitting are synonyms, both meaning suitable or appropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Make a fuss in front of awful island houses

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
the island holds the other letter inside it as a house holds its occupants

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss about the dreadful houses on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To create, in informal British usage, is to complain loudly or kick up a row.

clue.text: Bailiff seizes pair, one let off

indicators.note: the officer grabs the other letters and holds them inside

blocks.note: a reeve was a medieval steward or bailiff

explanation.surface: A bailiff seizes two people, but one of them is released.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a medieval English official who managed an estate for its lord, an old word setters use for a bailiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a cancellation or postponement of punishment, the state of someone who has been excused.

clue.text: Remember inconclusive direction, one in a Shakespeare play

indicators.note: without a conclusion, the word for direction loses its ending
the one is placed inside the play's abbreviation

blocks.note: a bearing is a compass direction
short for A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Someone recalls vague stage directions given to an actor in a Shakespeare production.
explanation.walkthrough: BEARING loses its G, and I goes inside MND, the usual shorthand for A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear in mind is an idiom for keeping something in your thoughts and not forgetting it.

clue.text: Amazing reductions at start of day, but not one for DIYers?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the noun phrase

indicators.note: amazing suggests the letters are thrown into bewildering disorder
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shop advertises fantastic sales first thing in the morning, but warns that they are not aimed at home improvers.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY means do-it-yourself home improvement; amateurs pay retail, while professional builders get the trade price.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade discount is a price cut given only to businesses and tradespeople, so an amateur doing their own repairs misses out.

clue.text: Monk peaceful to hear, taking cream

indicators.note: to hear means the word for peaceful is judged by its sound, not spelling

blocks.note: calm and carm sound the same in non-rhotic British speech
the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: A tranquil monk, by the sound of it, helps himself to cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carmelite is a friar of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, a Catholic religious order.

clue.text: Boring way to transfer funds over, but one draws from it

indicators.note: turned over, the words before it are read upwards in this down answer

blocks.note: BACS is the British automated bank payment system

explanation.surface: A dull method of moving money abroad, yet someone takes cash out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAB plus BACS reversed gives SCAB-BARD. BACS (Bankers' Automated Clearing Services) handles UK direct debits and wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath for a sword, and a swordsman draws his blade out of it.

clue.text: Rural rail line a fine thing at first

indicators.note: says the fine thing is placed at the beginning, ahead of the other pieces

blocks.note: a cracker is an informal word for something excellent

explanation.surface: A countryside railway line is praised as a fine thing from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail line' looks like a railway, but rail is a ballet barre and line is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracker-barrel describes homespun country wisdom, from the barrel of crackers round which store customers chatted in rural America.

clue.text: Foolish king within almost too attentive

indicators.note: the king is placed inside the other piece
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: King Lear foolishly divides his kingdom

explanation.surface: A silly monarch is nearly too eager to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSO loses its O to give ALS, which holds LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: All ears is an idiom for listening eagerly and giving full attention to a speaker.

clue.text: Drained lake, every weed regularly pulled out

indicators.note: pulling out at regular intervals removes every other letter, leaving the rest

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of weed

explanation.surface: A gardener empties a lake, tugging out all the weed at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Leached describes liquid having seeped or been drawn out of a substance, so the material has been emptied.

clue.text: Cat taking advantage of medic?

blocks.note: a user is someone who takes advantage

explanation.surface: A cat seems to be exploiting the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as MO-USER, someone who uses the medic.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept for, or skilled at, catching rodents around a house or farm.

clue.text: Black cats on island left in large numbers

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after, so the big cats follow

explanation.surface: Black cats are found on an island where they have been left in great numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A billion is a thousand million, so billions are vast quantities in the plural.

clue.text: Work out with hellish new gangster away

indicators.note: sent away, these letters are removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: Detectives deduce something about a fiendish new mobster who has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or conclude from evidence, reasoning your way to a conclusion.

clue.text: Turned a limb to ice

indicators.note: turned round, the phrase for a limb is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Something like a limb is turned to ice, as if frozen solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian ice cream, and an ice is a frozen dessert of that sort.

clue.text: Principal elements of strategy youth never could coordinate

indicators.note: the principal or leading element of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A strategy that young people were never able to organise properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sync is to synchronise, making things happen in step at the same time.

clue.text: I’m surprised garden barrier’s lost a little height

indicators.note: having lost something, the barrier word is missing one letter

blocks.note: a ha-ha is a sunken fence or ditch bounding a landscaped garden
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Someone is startled that their garden fence has shrunk slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: HAHA drops its first H, leaving AHA. A ha-ha is a British landscape-garden feature: a ditch with a wall that keeps livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is an exclamation of sudden realisation or surprise, the sort of interjection a startled speaker blurts out.

clue.text: Filthy rag is smudging party decorations

indicators.note: smudging blurs and messes up, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grubby cloth leaves smears on the decorations put up for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings of small coloured electric bulbs are hung up as festive ornaments at celebrations.

clue.text: Wanted to be free of parent?

blocks.note: second, playful meaning: having the sire, or father, taken away, as de- removes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a sire is a parent, and the prefix de- means removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired means wished for or craved, while the split reading imagines someone who has been relieved of a father.

clue.text: Finally ad caused a run on revolutionary mousetrap?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the following two words
in an across answer, on means placed after, so these letters follow the revolutionary

blocks.note: last letters of ad and caused
abbreviation for a run in cricket scores

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a radical new mousetrap causes a rush of buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mousetrap is old British slang for cheap cheese, the kind set as bait in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is the commonest hard English cheese, just the sort of thing baited in traps for rodents.
